subject: Post-demo: deployment decision criteria & hosted trial checklist
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-09T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: deployment decision criteria & hosted trial checklist

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum while you evaluate deployment options (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

Summary of what we discussed
- Primary goal: integrate summarization + entity extraction into your claims intake flow (low-latency, multitenant data segregation).
- Traffic profile: avg 60 reqs/minute during business hours, spiky bursts to ~400 reqs/min for 10–15 minutes.
- Data sensitivity: PII in text but encrypted at rest is acceptable; SOC2 + audit logs required.

Recommended quick evaluation: start with a Hosted API trial configured to mirror your peak concurrency so we can validate latency & cost without infra commitment. Hosted will let you test our autoscaling, prefix caching, and endpoint throttling quickly. If you hit constraints, we can map to Dedicated with reserved GPU pools. Private/VPC will be the final step if you need customer-managed network + HSM.

Action items (proposed)
1) We'll provision a Hosted trial project with two endpoints: low-latency (gpt-large-lite quantized) and accuracy (gpt-large-fp16). Please confirm a sample dataset (<= 5k documents) to push for warmup.
2) We’ll set rate caps to mirror your stated bursts (start with 500 req/min global; token-based soft limits). We’ll share an ops playbook for throttling behavior.
3) Security: we’ll enable role-based keys and turn on audit logs. If you need VPC, list required IP ranges and we’ll scope the Private path.

Attachments: Hosted-Quickstart-Checklist.pdf (quick steps + config), FinLytics-Data-Profile.xlsx (we can use this to estimate token mix).

Questions for you
- Can you confirm the sample dataset and whether redaction can be performed before sending to the trial endpoints?
- Any hard requirements around regional residency (US-only) or specific SLA numbers?

Proposed next meeting: 30 minutes on Wednesday to confirm dataset and provisioning windows. I’ll loop in Marissa for provisioning.

Thanks —
Rafael
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.ai
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@finlytics.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment decision criteria & hosted trial checklist

Rafael —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few quick points from our side: 

- Dataset: we can provide a 2k-sample CSV with invoices and claim notes. Redaction is possible but adds a manual step; prefer testing as-is if you support field-level masking on ingest.
- Residency: US-only is preferred for now.
- SLA: we need 99.9% uptime for production, but for the trial we just want to validate latency and throughput.

A couple of technical questions: 
1) What exactly happens when the Hosted trial hits the 500 req/min cap? Is there a queue, an HTTP 429, or graceful backpressure?
2) Can you give a ballpark for per-1k-token cost on the quantized low-latency endpoint vs the fp16 accuracy endpoint during trial?

If Hosted behaves well on throttling and latency, we’ll be comfortable continuing there for an initial prod slice; Dedicated/Private would be considered if we need stricter network controls or long-term reserved throughput.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Head of Platform
FinLytics
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-10T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment decision criteria & hosted trial checklist

Thanks Sanjay — good questions. Quick answers and specifics so your team can decide quickly:

1) Throttling behavior: by default the Hosted endpoints enforce token-based soft limits. During the trial we configure a global soft cap at 500 req/min which will return an HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header when exceeded. We can optionally enable a short request queue (up to 30s) for canary traffic — useful for bursty workloads. We’ll document how to handle 429s in the ops playbook.

2) Cost guidance (trial rates, ballpark):
- Quantized low-latency endpoint (gpt-large-lite-q8): ~ $0.40 per 1k input + output tokens.
- fp16 accuracy endpoint (gpt-large-fp16): ~ $1.20 per 1k tokens.
These are trial estimates; Dedicated reserved pricing reduces unit cost significantly once you commit to capacity. We’ll put together a simple cost calculator after we have your sample token mix.

Other notes:
- Residency: we’ll provision the trial in a US region and mark data residency controls accordingly.
- Security: audit logs and RBAC will be enabled by default for the trial. If you need HSM keywrap, that’s on the Private/VPC path.

Next steps (from our side)
- Marissa will provision the trial project and share endpoint URLs + API keys (short-lived) once you confirm the sample dataset.
- I’ll send the ops playbook with retry patterns and a sample client config.

Would Wednesday 11:00am PT work for a short provisioning sync?

— Rafael
